# State Transfer (Fetch Protocol)

State transfer is the recovery path that brings a replica back into consensus after it has fallen behind the cluster. The fallen replica pulls missing state from a peer via an incremental Merkle-tree walk: it requests a top-level `Meta_data` summary, compares the peer's subtree digests against its own, then descends only into mismatched subtrees until reaching leaf-level `Data` messages that overwrite individual state blocks. The fetch mechanism is implemented in `src/tbft_state.h`/`src/tbft_state.c` and `src/tbft_partition.h`/`src/tbft_partition.c`.

## Overview

State transfer is invoked when a replica determines that it is missing committed history (e.g. after a partition, a long sleep, or a view change in which it was not a participant). The fallen replica picks a `fetch_replier` (a peer replica believed to have stable state at some seqno `s`) and starts a recursive descent over the Merkle partition tree. At each level the replier sends a `Meta_data` carrying the digests of `TBFT_P_CHILDREN` children; the fetcher enqueues the children whose digests do not match its local copy. The walk terminates at the leaf level, where `Data` messages are verified by SHA-256 and written directly into the state buffer. Completion is signalled by `tbft_state_fetch_complete`.

The protocol is bounded by `TBFT_MAX_STATE_BLOCKS * 2` outstanding fetch requests (see `fetch_queue[]`) and `TBFT_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT_US` (initial value set in `tbft_state_init`, see `src/tbft_state.c:72`).

## When State Transfer Triggers (`in_fetch` Detection)

The boolean flag `tbft_state_t::in_fetch` is the single source of truth for "fetch in progress". It is set to `true` only by `tbft_state_start_fetch` (`src/tbft_state.c:293`) and cleared by `tbft_state_fetch_complete` (`src/tbft_state.c:480`).

```c
static inline bool tbft_state_in_fetch(const tbft_state_t *state)
{
    return state->in_fetch;
}
```

Source: `src/tbft_state.h:173-176`.

The replica layer calls `tbft_state_in_fetch` and `tbft_state_fetch_timedout` (defined inline at `src/tbft_state.h:182-186`) on every loop iteration. When `in_fetch == true`, the replica's `tbft_replica_run()` loop dispatches incoming `Meta_data` and `Data` messages to the fetch handlers instead of the normal BFT path. A timed-out fetch logs a warning and the replica either re-starts fetch with a different replier or stalls, depending on policy.

Common triggers in the replica layer:

| Trigger | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Recovery after view change | New primary may not have all history; initiates fetch from a peer |
| Replica joins after a long partition | `last_stable` lags behind cluster; must pull state up to `last_stable` |
| Detected gap in seqno range | Replica cannot execute until missing seqnos are recovered |

## `tbft_state_start_fetch` — Entry Point

Declared at `src/tbft_state.h:150-151`, implemented at `src/tbft_state.c:290-328`.

```c
void tbft_state_start_fetch(tbft_state_t *state, tbft_seqno_t seqno,
                            int replier);
```

Behaviour:

1. Resets fetch bookkeeping: `in_fetch = true`, `fetch_seqno = seqno`, `fetch_replier = replier`, `fetch_queue_len = 0`, `n_data_pending = 0`.
2. Initializes the timeout (`fetch_timeout_us = TBFT_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT_US` if not already set) and records `fetch_start_time_us = esp_timer_get_time()`.
3. Clears the fetch-received bitmap via `fetch_received_zero(state)`.
4. Branches on the partition tree depth (`src/tbft_state.c:308-324`):
   - **`p_levels == 1`**: The tree has no internal nodes (every block is a leaf with no parent). For each block `i` in `[0, num_blocks)`, enqueue a direct leaf-level data fetch `(level=0, index=i)`. `n_data_pending` is **not** incremented here; it is bumped later by `tbft_state_next_fetch_req` when it dequeues a leaf-level request (see `src/tbft_state.c:462-469`).
   - **`p_levels > 1`**: Enqueue a single root-level meta-data fetch `(level=0, index=0)`.

```c
if (state->ptree.dims.p_levels == 1) {
    for (int i = 0; i < state->num_blocks; i++) {
        if (state->fetch_queue_len >= (TBFT_MAX_STATE_BLOCKS * 2)) break;
        state->fetch_queue[state->fetch_queue_len].level = 0;
        state->fetch_queue[state->fetch_queue_len].index = i;
        state->fetch_queue[state->fetch_queue_len].done  = false;
        state->fetch_queue_len++;
    }
} else {
    state->fetch_queue[0].level = 0;
    state->fetch_queue[0].index = 0;
    state->fetch_queue[0].done  = false;
    state->fetch_queue_len      = 1;
}
```

The choice of replier is made by the caller (the replica layer); this function only stores the choice in `fetch_replier`.

## Merkle Partition Tree (`tbft_ptree_t`)

The partition tree is a multi-ary Merkle tree over state blocks. Defined in `src/tbft_partition.h:73-86`:

```c
typedef struct {
    tbft_ptree_dims_t dims;
    tbft_part_t  *ptree[TBFT_P_LEVELS];   /* per-level array of (digest, version) */
    tbft_dsum_t  *stree[TBFT_P_LEVELS];   /* per-level array of child digests sums */
    tbft_part_t  *ptree_mem;              /* backing storage (one alloc) */
    tbft_dsum_t  *stree_mem;
    int           total_nodes;
} tbft_ptree_t;
```

### Levels and Children per Node

- `TBFT_P_LEVELS` (Kconfig, default 4) caps the number of levels.
- `TBFT_P_CHILDREN` (Kconfig) is the branching factor; derived as `2 ^ TBFT_P_CHILDREN_LOG2` and asserted to be a power of 2 in `tbft_config.h`.
- `tbft_ptree_compute_levels(num_blocks, p_children)` (`src/tbft_partition.c:10-23`) returns the minimum number of levels to cover `num_blocks` leaves. If it exceeds `TBFT_P_LEVELS`, `tbft_ptree_init` returns `-1`.
- `tbft_ptree_nodes_at_level(level, p_children)` (`src/tbft_partition.c:29-37`) returns `p_children ^ level`, with a 1,000,001 overflow sentinel.
- The root sits at `ptree[0][0]`; leaves at `ptree[PLevels-1][i]` for `i ∈ [0, num_blocks)`.

### Per-Level Digests

Each node is a `tbft_part_t` (`src/tbft_partition.h:26-29`):

```c
typedef struct {
    tbft_digest_t  digest;    /* 32-byte SHA-256 */
    tbft_seqno_t   version;   /* seqno of last checkpoint that changed this node */
} tbft_part_t;
```

`tbft_ptree_update_leaf` (`src/tbft_partition.c:97-170`) recomputes the leaf digest and propagates the change upward. At each level it uses `psa_hash_setup` / `psa_hash_update` / `psa_hash_finish` to build the parent digest as `SHA256(child_0.digest || child_1.digest || … || child_{k-1}.digest)`. Hash failures abort with `-1` (H5 fix) rather than corrupting the tree.

The `stree[]` (digest-sum) arrays are allocated alongside `ptree[]` but the current update path uses concatenate-then-hash (not XOR-then-hash) — see comment at `src/tbft_partition.c:123-126` — so `stree[]` is reserved for future incremental updates and is not currently written.

### ASCII Diagram: Partition Tree for `P_LEVELS=4`, `P_CHILDREN=4`

With `TBFT_P_CHILDREN=4` and `TBFT_P_LEVELS=4`, a 4-level tree covers up to `4^3 = 64` leaf blocks (i.e. `num_blocks <= 64`):

```
                    ptree[0]
                   +--------+
                   | root   |   <-- level 0 (root)
                   | digest |
                   +--------+
                    /  |  |  \
        +----------/---+--+--\----------+
        |          |       |    |        |
   +--------+ +--------+ +--------+ +--------+
   | L1[0]  | | L1[1]  | | L1[2]  | | L1[3]  |   <-- level 1
   +--------+ +--------+ +--------+ +--------+
     / | \      / | \      / | \      / | \
    /  |  \    /  |  \    /  |  \    /  |  \
   /   |   \  /   |   \  /   |   \  /   |   \
  +--+ +--+ ++--+ +--+ ++--+ +--+ ++--+ +--+    <-- level 2 (internal)
  |  | |  | ||  | |  | ||  | |  | ||  | |  |
  +--+ +--+ ++--+ +--+ ++--+ +--+ ++--+ +--+
  |  | |  | ||  | |  | ||  | |  | ||  | |  |
  +--+ +--+ ++--+ +--+ ++--+ +--+ ++--+ +--+    <-- level 3 (LEAVES)
  B0 B1 B2 B3 B4 B5 B6 B7 B8 ...  B60 B61 B62 B63

  level 0: 1 node
  level 1: 4 nodes
  level 2: 16 nodes
  level 3: 64 nodes (TBFT_MAX_STATE_BLOCKS upper bound)
```

For larger `num_blocks`, `tbft_ptree_compute_levels` would return a level count > 4 — the caller must then raise `TBFT_P_LEVELS` or shrink the state. In the default counter example with `TBFT_MAX_STATE_BLOCKS=256`, four levels are insufficient and `TBFT_P_LEVELS` is raised in `sdkconfig.defaults`.

`tbft_ptree_root_digest(tree)` (inline at `src/tbft_partition.h:112-116`) returns `&tree->ptree[0][0].digest` — the overall state digest. This root is what gets committed into `tbft_ckpt_record_t::root_digest` on each checkpoint (`src/tbft_state.c:224`).

## Fetch → Meta_data → Data Flow

The fetch protocol is a two-phase recursive walk.

```
fetcher                                          replier
  |                                                |
  |--- Fetch(root, level=0, index=0) ------------>|
  |                                                |
  |<-- Meta_data(level=0,index=0,digest_0..3) -----|
  |   (d_i = SHA256 of each child subtree)         |
  |                                                |
  | for each child i:                              |
  |   if local ptree[1][i].digest != d_i:          |
  |     enqueue Fetch(level=1, index=i)            |
  |                                                |
  |--- Fetch(level=1, index=2) ------------------->|
  |<-- Meta_data(level=1,index=2, digest_0..3) ----|
  |   ...recursive descent...                      |
  |                                                |
  |--- Fetch(level=3, index=42) ------------------>|
  |<-- Data(level=3,index=42, block_bytes, d) -----|
  |   verify: SHA256(block_bytes) == d             |
  |   memcpy into state->mem + 42*TBFT_BLOCK_SIZE  |
  |   update ptree leaf                            |
  |   fetch_received[42] = 1                       |
  |   n_data_pending--                             |
```

### Meta_data Handler: `tbft_state_handle_meta_data`

Implementation: `src/tbft_state.c:330-397`.

1. Drop the message if `!in_fetch` or `rep->seqno != fetch_seqno`.
2. Bounds-check `level ∈ [0, p_levels-2)` (Meta_data is only valid for non-leaf levels).
3. Bounds-check `index ∈ [0, nodes_at_level(level))` to prevent OOB indexing of `ptree[level][index]`.
4. Bounds-check `n_parts ∈ [0, pchildren]`.
5. For each child `i ∈ [0, n_parts)`:
   - Compute `child_idx = index * pchildren + i` and bounds-check.
   - Read local digest `local = &ptree[child_level][child_idx].digest`.
   - If `local != parts[i].digest`, enqueue `(child_level, child_idx)` into `fetch_queue[]` (capped at `TBFT_MAX_STATE_BLOCKS * 2`).

The function does not differentiate between leaf and internal children; `tbft_state_next_fetch_req` checks `level == p_levels - 1` to decide whether to bump `n_data_pending` (`src/tbft_state.c:462-469`).

### Data Handler: `tbft_state_handle_data`

Implementation: `src/tbft_state.c:399-453`.

1. Drop the message if `!in_fetch` or `rep->seqno != fetch_seqno`.
2. Bounds-check `block_index ∈ [0, num_blocks)`.
3. Deduplicate: `if (fetch_received_test(bidx)) return;` (the bitmap `fetch_received[]` prevents retransmits from double-decrementing `n_data_pending`).
4. Compute `SHA256(block_data)` and compare with `rep->digest`. On mismatch, log a warning and return without writing.
5. On match: `memcpy` into `state->mem + bidx * TBFT_BLOCK_SIZE`, update `state->block_digests[bidx]`, and call `tbft_ptree_update_leaf` to propagate upward.
6. Mark `fetch_received[bidx] = 1` and decrement `n_data_pending` (clamped at 0).
7. If all fetch_queue entries are `done` **and** `n_data_pending == 0`, call `tbft_state_fetch_complete`.

### `tbft_state_next_fetch_req`

Implementation: `src/tbft_state.c:455-475`. Scans `fetch_queue[]` for the first not-done entry, marks it done, returns `(level, index)`. For leaf-level requests, it increments `n_data_pending` only if the block has not already arrived out-of-order (`if (!fetch_received_test(state, *index))`).

## CoW Bitmap (`cowb[]` — Multi-Word)

`cowb` is **not** a single 64-bit bitmap — it is a multi-word array sized for the maximum number of state blocks.

Source: `src/tbft_state.h:50`:

```c
tbft_bitmap_t cowb[TBFT_MAX_STATE_BLOCKS / 64 + 1];
```

Helpers in `src/tbft_state.c:12-25`:

| Helper | Behaviour |
|--------|-----------|
| `cow_set(s, i)` | `s->cowb[i / 64] \|= 1ULL << (i % 64)` |
| `cow_test(s, i)` | Returns bit `i % 64` of word `i / 64` |
| `cow_zero(s)` | `memset(s->cowb, 0, sizeof(s->cowb))` |

Bit `i` is set when block `i` is snapshotted into the active checkpoint's `old_blocks[]` array (see `tbft_state_cow_single` at `src/tbft_state.c:135-170`). The bitmap is reset (`cow_zero`) at the end of every successful `tbft_state_checkpoint` (`src/tbft_state.c:229`) and on rollback (`src/tbft_state.c:262`).

The companion bitmap `fetch_received[]` (declared at `src/tbft_state.h:72`) uses the same multi-word scheme to track which leaf blocks have been received during the current fetch; helpers `fetch_received_set` / `fetch_received_test` / `fetch_received_zero` are at `src/tbft_state.c:31-44`.

## `block_digests[]` — Per-Block SHA-256

```c
tbft_digest_t block_digests[TBFT_MAX_STATE_BLOCKS];
```

Source: `src/tbft_state.h:56`. One SHA-256 digest (32 bytes) per state block. Updated:

- On checkpoint — `tbft_state_checkpoint` recomputes the digest of every block whose `cowb` bit is set, then propagates upward via `tbft_ptree_update_leaf` (`src/tbft_state.c:202-213`).
- On rollback — `tbft_state_rollback` rebuilds the leaf digest after restoring the snapshot (`src/tbft_state.c:252-259`).
- On fetch — `tbft_state_handle_data` writes the new digest after verifying the block (`src/tbft_state.c:426`).

`block_digests[]` is the leaf layer of the partition tree; the parent digests in `ptree[level < p_levels-1][]` are derived from these.

## `ckpt_records[]` — `TBFT_NUM_CKPT_SLOTS`

```c
tbft_ckpt_record_t ckpt_records[TBFT_NUM_CKPT_SLOTS];
int                ckpt_head;   /* index of oldest valid record */
int                ckpt_count;
```

Source: `src/tbft_state.h:59-61`. The struct itself is at `src/tbft_state.h:28-34`:

```c
typedef struct {
    tbft_seqno_t    seqno;
    tbft_digest_t   root_digest;
    tbft_cow_entry_t *old_blocks;     /* heap array of block snapshots */
    int              num_old_blocks;
    bool             valid;
} tbft_ckpt_record_t;
```

`TBFT_NUM_CKPT_SLOTS` is derived in `tbft_config.h` as `TBFT_WINDOW_SIZE / TBFT_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL + 1` (the `+1` covers the slot in active use at the window head).

### Slot Addressing

`ckpt_slot_for(s, seqno)` (`src/tbft_state.c:50-54`) computes:

```c
int slot = (int)((seqno / TBFT_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL) % TBFT_NUM_CKPT_SLOTS);
```

### Pre-Allocation

`tbft_state_init` pre-allocates a `tbft_cow_entry_t` array of `num_blocks` entries for **every** slot (`src/tbft_state.c:91-107`). This is a hard upper bound — every block can change at most once per checkpoint interval — and avoids `realloc()` in the CoW hot path.

### Retention

`tbft_state_checkpoint` (line 222-226) writes `seqno`, `root_digest`, and `valid` into the slot but does **not** free `old_blocks` (the snapshots are needed for rollback during view-change). The pre-allocated array is reused across cycles. `tbft_state_mark_stable` (`src/tbft_state.c:266-284`) unconditionally resets `num_old_blocks = 0` and zeroes the storage for the now-stable slot.

### Lookup

`tbft_state_get_checkpoint_digest(state, seqno, &out)` (`src/tbft_state.c:486-499`) returns `true` and copies the root digest if the slot is `valid && rec->seqno == seqno`. This is the API the view-change protocol uses to attach the digests of recent stable checkpoints to `View_change` messages.

## `last_stable` Tracking

`tbft_seqno_t last_stable` (`src/tbft_state.h:75`) is the highest seqno for which a stable checkpoint has been observed. It is updated only by `tbft_state_mark_stable(state, stable_seqno)` (`src/tbft_state.c:266-284`):

```c
void tbft_state_mark_stable(tbft_state_t *state, tbft_seqno_t stable_seqno)
{
    if (stable_seqno <= state->last_stable) return;
    tbft_ckpt_record_t *new_rec = ckpt_slot_for(state, stable_seqno);
    if (new_rec->old_blocks) {
        new_rec->num_old_blocks = 0;
        memset(new_rec->old_blocks, 0,
               (size_t)state->num_blocks * sizeof(tbft_cow_entry_t));
    }
    state->last_stable = stable_seqno;
}
```

The function is monotonic — a smaller `stable_seqno` is a no-op. The reset of `num_old_blocks` is critical: a slot that was only a CoW target (not a checkpoint target) for a previous `last_stable` could carry stale `old_blocks` into the new cycle; the unconditional zero prevents that.

`last_stable` is the seqno returned by `tbft_state_rollback` (`src/tbft_state.c:237-264`) and is the address used by `ckpt_slot_for` to find the active CoW target in `tbft_state_cow_single` (`src/tbft_state.c:141`).

## v0.7.2 Fix: Removed 4×WINDOW Limit on State Fetch

Commit `c937fbe` ("v0.7.2-state-transfer-fix: remove 4×WINDOW limit on state fetch") removed a cap on how far ahead of `last_stable` a fetch could be initiated. Prior to the fix, the replica layer rejected `tbft_state_start_fetch` calls whose target `seqno` exceeded `last_stable + 4 * WINDOW_SIZE` — a heuristic that prevented a freshly-joined replica from ever catching up to a cluster that had advanced by more than four windows. The fix removed this cap; the fetch protocol now uses only `TBFT_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT_US` (set in `tbft_state_init`) to bound the operation. The `fetch_queue[]` cap of `TBFT_MAX_STATE_BLOCKS * 2` remains as a queue-depth safeguard, not a correctness limit.
